generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential from 1; never NULL; unique per table; never targeted by duplicate planting or group-size planting.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Sample from the final parent PK pool (after all parent dedupe and NULL planting); 5-30% NULL only where the column is nullable; otherwise always a valid parent key. Re-validate FK after all planting.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_short: Random word-like token 3-20 chars; 5% near-variant (case flip, trailing space, doubled char) of a pool literal.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_name: Random capitalized given/surname from a 40-name pool; 5% near-variant (lowercase, typo) of a pool literal.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_address: Number + street word + suffix; city/state/country from small pools.
generic_sampling_rules.varchar_phone: Random digits with optional +, -, (), x separators, 10-15 chars.
generic_sampling_rules.double_amount: Uniform 0..10000 with 2 decimals; 5-30% NULL where nullable.
generic_sampling_rules.enum_short: Pick uniformly from the column's enum list.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_numeric: For each listed literal L, include L, L-step, L+step where step is 1 for integers and 0.01 for doubles.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_text: For each listed literal L, include L and a case-variant (lower/upper) and a one-char typo.
generic_sampling_rules.boundary_date: For each listed literal L, include L, L-1 day, L+1 day in the column format.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicates_for_distinct: Ensure 20-50% of non-NULL values repeat an earlier value in the same column; never applied to primary-key columns.
generic_sampling_rules.ties_for_order_limit: Ensure at least 3 rows share the same value at the listed ORDER rank.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, 5-30% of rows NULL; at least one NULL per nullable column per instance; never applied to PK columns; applied exactly once per column (FK NULL path or generic path, not both).
generic_sampling_rules.group_sizes: Ensure groups of size 1, 2 and >=3 exist on the grouped column; applied to the final column values after all planting; never applied to a primary-key column.
generic_sampling_rules.unmatched_join_rows: For each join column, ensure at least one parent row has no child and at least one child FK points to a valid parent (no orphan unless nullable). For NOT NULL child FKs, achieve parent-childlessness by redirecting/removing child rows, never by setting the FK to NULL.
generic_sampling_rules.aggregate_boundary: For each listed aggregate target, plant child-row counts so that COUNT(*) and COUNT(col) take the values 1, 2 and >=3 across parent groups; NULLs in the counted column reduce COUNT(col) but not COUNT(*); use the instance rng for parent selection; preserve planted NULLs in the counted column.

uncertainty: table_sizes_per_instance counts GENERATED rows appended to the compact database, not total rows. The compact DB already has 3 Vehicles rows, so the final Vehicles table has 3 compact + 6 generated = 9 rows; the 6 generated rows are needed to make group_sizes (1,2,>=3) on vehicle_details achievable.
No formula relates amount_outstanding to payments or lesson price; none is stated.
lesson_time is a free-form VARCHAR(10); boundary values '' and 'x' are targeted and the column is also nullable, so boundary literals appear among non-NULL rows and NULLs are planted separately.

Customer_Payments composite PK (customer_id, datetime_payment) is enforced by generation order and unique datetime per customer; datetime_payment is sampled per customer with uniqueness; composite PK dedupe must not drop rows needed for aggregate-boundary planting.
Staff.date_of_birth values in the sample include minors (2010-2015); no age constraint is asserted, and no minimum-age is intended.
No FK enforcement is enabled in the writer; FK targets are sampled from the final parent PK pool after all dedupe and NULL planting, and a post-generation FK validation is required.
Duplicate planting is applied to primary-key columns only where the final PK is not required to be unique; the program should dedupe PKs after planting and re-validate FK references.
The instance file is the compact database plus appended generated rows; the original DB path must be passed through to the writer so compact rows are copied.

Aggregate-boundary targets (COUNT(*) > 2 with counts 1,2,>=3) must be planted explicitly for Customers.customer_id and Customer_Payments.customer_id/amount_payment; the parent-side group sizes (Customers.customer_id) must take 1, 2 and >=3 across the full parent set, not just 3 parents with 1/2/3 and the rest 0.

Customers.customer_id group_sizes is achieved via the child-side (Customer_Payments.customer_id) distribution, not by planting duplicates on the PK column; _plant_group_sizes must never be applied to a primary-key column.

Nullable FK NULL share must be computed once from _null_share(rng) and applied as a single target count; the previous double mechanism (0.15 pre-threshold plus _plant_nulls) could exceed the 5-30% cap. Lessons.staff_id is handled solely by the FK NULL path and must be removed from NULL_SHARE_COLUMNS.
Each nullable column must receive at least one NULL per instance; a post-generation assertion should verify this across all instances.
The lesson_date >= '2015-01-01' rule is removed from semantic_rules_and_formulas; the DateSampler range (2015-01-01..2018-03-31) already satisfies it by construction.

The writer should enable foreign_keys=ON before any transaction (or run PRAGMA foreign_key_check after commit) and raise on violations; generated parent PKs must be a superset of the original PKs so compact child rows still resolve.
The writer should open the compact DB read-only and use the sqlite3 backup API or VACUUM INTO to create a consistent copy, or ensure the original is not in WAL mode.

max_l0 in the sampler must be at least 3 for columns in GROUP_SIZE_COLUMNS and large enough for 20-50% duplicates on DUPLICATE_COLUMNS, so that group_sizes and duplicates_for_distinct targets remain achievable.

After fixing aggregate-boundary and group-size planting, re-run the construction check and verify that construction_pairs_by_group is populated and separated count increases; add a post-generation assertion that for each AGGREGATE_BOUNDARY triple, the child-row counts per parent include 1, 2 and >=3, and that COUNT(counted_col) also includes 1, 2 and >=3.
